Phlegmanol C, a compound that binds to this enzyme, is implicated in the inhibition of T-24 cells, a type of human bladder cancer cell line. The presence of a well-documented interaction between 25-Hydroxy-3-Epidehydrotumulosic Acid and Phlegmanol C, along with the observed effect on T-24 cells, supports a mechanistic link between the compound and the disease. The integration of these pathways highlights the potential for 25-Hydroxy-3-Epidehydrotumulosic Acid to modulate cellular metabolism in T-24 cells through the inhibition of Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, thereby influencing cancer progression.
